title: Retry and time out a protocol step
description: A transient step failure today costs a whole performance: the only recovery is diagnosis leading to reperform or recast, which was designed for structural failure rather than a flaky call. ProtocolStep has no retry and no timeout. Add both plus StageOptions defaults, and make every attempt visible in the trace so flakiness cannot hide behind a green run. A timeout turns a hanging step into a failed turn, which needs the abort signal -- hence the blocker.
acceptance_criteria: ProtocolStep.retry (attempts, backoff) and timeoutMs with stage-level defaults; each attempt records a trace event; a timed-out step yields a failed turn rather than a hang; optional and owns semantics preserved; R-STEP requirements and docs.
close_reason: ProtocolStep.retry/timeoutMs + StageOptions defaults; per-attempt AbortSignal; retried-away attempts are turns but not failures. R-STEP-RETRY-1..6, R-STEP-TIMEOUT-1..4; 216 tests / 0 fail; typecheck clean.

title: Pass an AbortSignal through a performance
description: drama has no cancellation: nothing in src/ mentions signal or abort. Every engine in the survey supports it, and it is a prerequisite for a step timeout that does not lie -- you cannot stop an in-flight model call, only abandon waiting for it. Smallest reversible design: StageOptions.signal, checked between waves, and the same signal exposed on ActorContext so an executor can abort its own transport call.
acceptance_criteria: StageOptions.signal stops a running performance between waves; executors receive it through ActorContext; an aborted performance ends in a distinct inspectable outcome rather than a throw; R-ABORT requirements and docs.
notes: Implemented in debe4a0. StageOptions.signal + ActorContext.signal; a new PerformanceStatus 'aborted' on the result and the finished event; canceled performances skip evaluation. R-ABORT-1..6 in test/requirements/abort.requirements.test.ts; full suite 206 pass / 0 fail, typecheck exit 0. Deliberate limit documented: the check is between waves, so casting/auditioning already ran.
close_reason: StageOptions.signal + ActorContext.signal implemented in debe4a0; R-ABORT-1..6 green; 206 tests / 0 fail; typecheck clean.

title: Correct and date-stamp the LangGraph recipe
description: docs/engines.md section 1 (lines 43-57) is the recipe the engine seam is demonstrated with, and no test or example ever executes it. Correct the drift the evaluation drama found, keep it a recipe (no adapter), and date-stamp it the way docs/prior-art.md stamps its snapshot.
acceptance_criteria: The recipe names @langchain/langgraph 1.4.18; createReactAgent is marked deprecated since at least 1.0.0 with the replacement createAgent from the langchain package (a third install beside the graph and provider packages); the Node note says @langchain/langgraph declares >=18 but the effective floor is 20, from @langchain/core and @langchain/anthropic; the .text trap is documented (empty string for tool-call or non-text finals, non-text blocks dropped) and structured output is steered to responseFormat plus result.structuredResponse with an explicit presence guard, cross-referencing drama-gas.4; a checked-against-versions-on-date line is added; every claim carries a source; git diff --name-only -- package.json is empty.
close_reason: docs/engines.md section 1 corrected and date-stamped: createAgent from the langchain package replaces the deprecated createReactAgent (three installs), the real Node 20 floor is stated, and the msg.text trap is documented with responseFormat/result.structuredResponse and an explicit presence guard, cross-referencing drama-gas.4. Checked 2026-09-27 UTC against @langchain/langgraph 1.4.18 / @langchain/anthropic 1.5.11 / @langchain/core 1.2.13, with a source per claim. Docs only: package.json untouched. No adapter, no dependency.

title: LangGraph integration: verified, not adapted
description:
Plan and evaluate the LangGraph integration. Verdict: do NOT add a LangGraph adapter or dependency; the createEngineExecutor seam (src/engines.ts) is sufficient and the stance in docs/prior-art.md:101-116 is correct. What the drama found is that the recipe demonstrating the seam is stale and hides one silent trap.

Drift, each verified against the current package:
- createReactAgent is deprecated (since at least @langchain/langgraph@1.0.0); the replacement is createAgent from the separate langchain package.
- The pin is one patch stale: @langchain/langgraph 1.4.17 -> 1.4.18.
- The documented Node 18+ is wrong in practice: @langchain/langgraph declares >=18, but @langchain/core and @langchain/anthropic declare >=20, so the effective floor is 20.
- .text is a real BaseMessage getter, but it returns an empty string for a tool-call or non-text final message and drops non-text blocks. Through the seam that becomes an artifact with empty content: a silent wrong answer, not a crash.
- The any-engine-works claim is only proven generically: R-ENGINE-1..5 inject a fake invoke, and nothing in the repo ever imports an engine package (package.json declares no dependencies).

Work is planned, not implemented: this epic was produced by the drama in examples/langgraph/run.ts.
acceptance_criteria: Each child meets its own acceptance criteria, bun test and bun run typecheck stay green, and git diff --name-only -- package.json is empty across all three.
close_reason: All three children are done: the recipe is corrected and date-stamped (.1), checked against the real package on demand via bun run verify:engines (.2), and the reverse direction is documented (.3). No adapter and no dependency was added; structured output and durable resume remain with drama-gas.4/.6.

title: Make a gated performance resumable
description: Approver is an in-process predicate (GateRequest) => boolean | Promise<boolean> and fails closed, so a gate with no human present simply halts the show. Durable suspend and resume is the one genuine advantage the surveyed engines have. drama is unusually well placed for it: the trace and the cast are data, and only executors are re-attached, as R-SERIAL-6 proves. Smallest reversible design to start from: pause at gate boundaries rather than after every turn, persist, and resume later with the approval.
acceptance_criteria: a gated performance can pause, persist, and resume to completion with the approval supplied afterwards; the paused state reuses the existing serialization; fail-closed behaviour is preserved when no approval ever arrives; requirements and docs.
close_reason: StageManager.resume + a new PerformanceStatus "paused": with no approver at all a REQUIRED gate pauses the show (finalResult.gate names the step) instead of failing a step nobody denied, and resume continues the same performance (same id, earlier turns and events kept) by re-entering the paused iteration and skipping steps that already have turns. The paused state is the ordinary Performance, so serializePerformance stores it and a reload resumes with executors re-attached by name (R-RESUME-1..6). A denial (an approver answering false, or throwing) still halts, an optional gate stays skippable, and resuming with nobody to answer pauses again — so an unanswered gate is never a pass. R-GUARD-2 revised (it asserted the old fail-with-failure outcome) and R-GUARD-11 added for the denial-is-not-a-pause rule. PERFORMANCE_FORMAT_VERSION 1 -> 2, since a new terminal status is a semantic change; older documents still load. bun test 235 -> 242; typecheck green; no dependency added.

title: Optional content contract for artifacts (structured output)
description: expectedOutput names artifact kinds, but the content is unguarded: the total-normalizer discipline stops at the card boundary. All five engines now support native structured output (Mastra structuredOutput, OpenAI response_format, Anthropic output_config.format with a JSON schema). Add an optional per-kind contract so createLlmExecutor can request and validate it. Zero-dependency constraint: accept a host-provided validator or a minimal subset. A validation failure must be a failed turn rather than a throw, so that it composes with retry.
acceptance_criteria: an actor can declare an artifact content contract; the LLM path validates it; a mismatch fails the turn with the validation error visible; no new runtime dependencies; requirements and docs.
close_reason: src/contract.ts: an optional per-kind content contract, either a declarative shape (type/required/fields/items, serialisable so a casting card can carry it as contentContract or content_contract) or a host check ((content) => true | reason, where a throw is a refusal and never escapes). Actor gained contentContract; renderActorPrompt renders the shape as a hint so a model can comply; createLlmExecutor validates the turn and a mismatch becomes failed(...) with the artifact kind and the failing path in the error, keeping the artifacts as evidence. R-CONTRACT-1..6 and docs. No runtime dependency (package.json, bun.lock and tsconfig untouched); bun test 229 -> 235; typecheck green.

title: Carry executor usage and support a cost budget
description: maxTurns counts executions, which is a poor proxy for cost: one turn with a large context can cost orders of magnitude more than another. The words usage and cost appear nowhere in src/. Engines expose usage in their responses, so passing it through is free. Side effect worth having: it also unblocks the WISE judge-panel stop rule (arXiv:2608.19802), which was declined in docs/graph-engineering.md precisely because drama had no cost data.
acceptance_criteria: ActorOutput.usage flows into ActorTurn and the trace without breaking serialization; StageOptions.maxCostUsd halts a performance like the other budgets; requirements and docs updated.
close_reason: ActorOutput.usage -> ActorTurn.usage; StageOptions.maxCostUsd checked between waves; unknown cost never trips it and usage survives serialization. R-COST-3..6; 220 tests / 0 fail; typecheck clean.

title: Borrow the missing agent-engine primitives
description: Close the gaps found comparing drama against the top-5 agent engines (LangGraph, OpenAI Agents SDK, Google ADK, CrewAI, Mastra), recorded in docs/prior-art.md. Every item is a primitive those engines treat as table stakes and drama lacks; nothing here is engine parity for its own sake, and the explicit non-goals (streaming, memory/RAG, MCP client, per-actor model routing, deployment) stay non-goals.
acceptance_criteria: Each child issue is implemented with R-id requirements per docs/requirements.md convention, the suite and typecheck are green, and docs are updated where behaviour is documented.

title: Document running a drama performance inside LangGraph
description: docs/engines.md only shows engine-into-actor. The reverse direction is missing and is free: an async StateGraph node can await a drama performance and return a partial state update. Document it, with a tool variant, and be precise about what the checkpointer can carry.
acceptance_criteria: Docs only; zero src/ change; it does not implement or close drama-gas.6. The recipe uses the real API: StageManager.run returns RunOutcome (a union of needs_input and performance, src/stage.ts:290-309), so the node handles the union and returns a partial update such as { performance }; a second variant shows the same call as a tool. The checkpointer note says the return must be serializable by the checkpointer serializer rather than strict JSON, and names UntrackedValue as the escape hatch. It states explicitly that persisting a drama performance under an engine checkpointer remains the specific project deferred in docs/prior-art.md:115-116.
close_reason: docs/engines.md gained 'The other direction: a performance inside an engine': a StateGraph node calling StageManager.run and handling the RunOutcome union (needs_input vs performance), the same call as a tool, and a source-checked table of what the checkpointer serializer keeps (Map/Set/Error/Uint8Array/RegExp/undefined revived; class instances flattened; functions dropped silently; cycles become '[Circular]'), with UntrackedValue named as the runtime-only channel. Both branches were exercised through a real StateGraph (@langchain/langgraph 1.4.18) while writing it. Docs only: no src/ change, and drama-gas.6 is explicitly not closed.

title: Add bun run verify:engines (LangGraph recipe check)
description: The only proof drama has of the seam is generic (a fake invoke). Add an on-demand check that installs the pinned LangGraph packages outside the repo, builds a minimal StateGraph with a fake chat model and runs it through createEngineExecutor, so recipe drift becomes a failing exit code instead of prose that quietly rots. LangGraph first; the other four recipes stay unverified.
acceptance_criteria: A docs-integrity checker, not a support commitment and not an adapter: it adds no package.json or tsconfig dependency and installs the pinned packages into an out-of-repo temp dir (~/.cache/drama/verify-engines) that can be deleted when it rots. It never statically imports an engine package (dynamic import from that temp dir), so tsc --noEmit stays green. It is not referenced by bun test or bun run typecheck and runs only as bun run verify:engines. It builds a minimal StateGraph with a fake chat model (no API key), invokes it through createEngineExecutor and asserts the artifact mapping. An install failure or API drift exits non-zero with a clear message. Scope is LangGraph only.
close_reason: scripts/verify-engines.ts + `bun run verify:engines` (PASS against @langchain/langgraph 1.4.18 / langchain 1.5.14 / @langchain/core 1.2.13 / zod 4.6.5): installs the pins into ~/.cache/drama/verify-engines (out-of-repo, DRAMA_VERIFY_ENGINES_DIR overridable), dynamically imports them through a generated shim, and checks createAgent, the graph exports, createAgent construction with responseFormat, a real StateGraph run under a fake model (no API key), the seam mapping to a RiskReport artifact, and the empty-answer guard. Failure modes tested: a stubbed package set produced 3 clear FAILs (exit 1), an unreachable registry produced a clear install message (exit 1). No dependency added (tsconfig and bun.lock untouched; package.json gained only the script), tsc green, bun test 229 pass and never touches it. LangGraph only; the other four recipes stay unchecked. Pin-vs-latest drift is a warning, not a failure, deliberately: patches ship every few days and failing on each would be noise.

title: Add a `decision` actor kind for calibrated decision models
description: Proposal from the Jev/Kev research in docs/decision-models.md. A System One / decision model takes a state plus typed questions and returns calibrated probabilities, no text. Minimal seam: add "decision" to ActorKind (src/actor.ts:14) and to actorFromCard's kind whitelist (src/cast.ts:345-348); carry the distribution as an Artifact. Non-goals: no `/v1/systemone` client or provider SDK in src/ (host-supplied DecisionFn like ChatFn), no "supported models" list, no new ActorOutput return shape.
acceptance_criteria: A R-DECISION-* requirement test proves a decision actor evaluates a criterion through a host-supplied DecisionFn and maps a calibrated probability to pass/fail/uncertain; demo in examples/decision-models/run.ts.
notes: Executed the drama through StageManager (examples/decision-models/run.ts): a full performance, 5 artifacts, evaluation pass, ZERO src/ change — the executor seam is kind-agnostic and criterionEvaluator composes. Recommendation sharpened: build the calibration policy (a provider-agnostic probability -> pass/fail/uncertain map at the Evaluator, ~20 lines beside criterionEvaluator, with an R-CALIB-* requirement test) FIRST; the 'decision' ActorKind is cosmetic today (kind only gates the card whitelist and the llm fallback) and should stay deferred until it has teeth. No /v1/systemone client or Distribution type in src/.
close_reason: Built: calibratedEvaluator + calibrate (src/evaluation.ts, R-CALIB-1..6) and the "decision" ActorKind + card whitelist (R-ACTOR-6); host-side adapter examples/providers/kev.ts + bun run setup:kev (R-KEV-1..3). No provider client or Distribution type in src/.

title: Export a performance trace as OpenTelemetry-shaped spans
description: ActorTurn already carries per-turn timings, status and actor identity, and performanceTimeline is essentially a span list, so this is an adapter rather than a core change. Emit OTLP-shaped JSON with zero dependencies and let the host export it. The structural fingerprint of R-DET-1 excludes timestamps, so determinism is unaffected.
acceptance_criteria: a function mapping a Performance to OTel-shaped spans; no new dependencies; deterministic for the same performance; requirements and docs.
